description: Bare technical checkpoint: runs the repository's official command suite and reports mechanical readiness, never literary quality.

text: TASK: certify the CURRENT WORK TREE at the scheduled full-suite checkpoint.
This is one fresh, report-only technical call. Determine the repository's official
complete suite when the operator has not supplied it, then run the ordered commands
at most once each, stop at the first failure, and report exactly what happened.
A passing suite establishes only declared mechanical readiness; it cannot certify
voice, character, continuity, pacing, theme, title quality, or editorial readiness.
- checkpoint: {{checkpoint_reason}}
OPERATOR-CONFIGURED MECHANICAL COMMANDS
{{verification_commands}}

variables.name: verification_commands
variables.default: (none — discover the official complete suite from repository-owned evidence)
variables.description: Ordered repository commands, one per line; when present they are authoritative and run separately in that order.

text: CHECKPOINT LAW
- You are not a manuscript author or editor: do not fix prose, code, tests,
configuration, or documents, and do not stage or commit. Only suite commands may
produce their ordinary generated or ignored outputs.
- Operator commands define this run's complete mechanical gate: execute exactly that
ordered list without narrowing, replacing, or supplementing it. Otherwise inspect
repository-owned CI, build, formatting, link, lint, test, and project documentation
to identify the official complete suite. Report the authority in `authority`.
- Run from the workspace root, non-interactively, with CI=1. Each command runs at most
once; never use watch mode, retry a failure, or call a no-op a passing suite.
- Block before running an interactive, watch-mode, or no-op operator command. Stop at
the first failure and report it without repair; the dedicated fixer receives the
command plan and complete actionable diagnostics.
- `no_suite` is legitimate only when no operator commands were supplied and repository
authorities establish that no complete mechanical suite exists. Cite that evidence.
- A passed command suite says nothing by itself about literary quality. If the official
suite is ambiguous or cannot be executed, return `blocked`; never guess or claim an
unrun command passed.

questions.status: bare technical kind — no battery by design

text: OUTPUT CONTRACT
Return exactly one JSON object, nothing else.
Passed or failed execution:
{"status":"passed"|"failed","kind":"suite_checkpoint",
"commands":["<ordered complete-suite command>",...],
"authority":{"source":"operator_config"|"repository",
"evidence":[{"path":"<workspace-relative path>",
"basis":"<what it establishes>"},...]},
"results":[{"command":"<attempted command>","exit_code":<integer>,
"evidence":"<concise output evidence>"},...],
"failure_account":{"command":"<failed command>",
"exit_code":<non-zero integer>,
"diagnostics":"<complete actionable failure output>",
"affected_tests":["<test id, if known>",...]}}
`commands` is the complete ordered plan; `results` contains exactly the
commands actually attempted, stopping at the first non-zero exit.
For `passed`, commands is non-empty, every command has one zero-exit result,
and the arrays have equal length. For `failed`, commands and results are
non-empty, results is the exact attempted prefix of commands, and its last
result has a non-zero exit; `failure_account` is then required and must match
that last result. Omit `failure_account` for `passed`.
With operator commands, `commands` equals that list exactly, `authority.source`
is `operator_config`, `authority.evidence` is empty, and `no_suite` is invalid.
Without them, source is `repository`, evidence is non-empty, and every
cited path must exist.
No suite exists:
{"status":"no_suite","kind":"suite_checkpoint",
"commands":[],"results":[],
"authority":{"source":"repository",
"evidence":[{"path":"<workspace-relative path>",
"basis":"<why it proves no suite exists>"},...]}}
Impossible checkpoint:
{"status":"blocked","kind":"suite_checkpoint",
"commands":["<resolved command, if any>",...],
"results":[<attempted results, if any>],
"blocked_reason":"<what prevented a trustworthy execution>"}
